newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger says NZ$1 bn cap on treaty claims gone.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger says NZ$1 bn cap on treaty claims gone.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Wednesday his party's NZ$1 billion "fiscal envelope" cap on Treaty of Waitangi settlements had been scrapped in a coalition deal with the nationalist New Zealand First Party.

The conservative National Party government had set aside NZ$1 billion over 10 years for settling claims. A major slice of the available funds has already been committed to a settlement with Tainui Maori in the centre of the North Island (NZ$170 million) and a settlement of fishing claims.
NZ First actively campaigned in the run-up to the election against the cap on settlement claim pay-outs.
Bolger was speaking shortly after his caretaker conservative National Party signed a coalition deal with the nationalist New Zealand First Party.
The deal, announced on Tuesday night, ended nearly two months of political suspense over who power-broker NZ First would choose as its coalition partner.
